verdict.rationale: Slate's docs describe running several agents in parallel from one TUI. They show as a grid of inline subagent cards, you can double-click a card to jump into that agent's session, and you can keep talking, queueing tasks or spinning up more agents while they run in the background. Separately, /sessions switches between existing sessions and Ctrl+X N opens a new one. missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of multi-session management, and documented controls for monitoring or stopping individual agents across sessions.

support.subject: As an engineering-lead, I can manage multiple agent-driven coding sessions from one unified workspace

citations.quote: Those agents show up as a grid of inline subagent cards, one per agent.
Double-click any card to jump into that agent's session and follow the full conversation.
While one or more agents run in the background, you can keep talking with Slate: plan next steps, queue up additional tasks, or spin up more agents to parallelize work across several tasks at once.
Use `/sessions` to switch between existing sessions
